To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of integral and differential features is beneficial to the evolution of accurate and predictive solutions for single-step time-series forecasting, and that rational features are beneficial for the evolution of accurate solutions for both single-step time-series and multi-step time- series forecasting.
The use of statistical analysis primitives in genetic programming is beneficial for the induction of accurate single-step predictors.

the use of the integral and differential primitives is beneficial in the induction of single-step predictors, whereas the use of the rational primitive is beneficial in the evolution of multi-step predictors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of genetic programming (GP) for time-series forecasting in a supply chain environment.
the development and evaluation of a genetic programming system for time-series predictors.

developing an understanding of the role that the primitives play in the evolution of accurate time-series predictors, and the extent to which they are able to capture the underlying dynamics of the time series.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of the rational transformation of the input time-series data is the best approach for single-step predictions, while the use of the differential transformation is best for multi-step predictions.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
genetic programming is capable of producing accurate and predictive models of supply chain data, and that it is capable of producing such models in a reasonable amount of time.
, for both single-step prediction and multi-step prediction, the best results are obtained when using the rational data transformation method.
the use of primitives that facilitate the calculation of statistical features of the input data is a promising direction for the evolution of time-series predictors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of statistical primitives in the evolved programs does not necessarily lead to more accurate solutions.
the use of primitives that perform statistical analysis on the input data is beneficial for forecasting in the supply chain management scenario considered in this paper.

, for multi-step prediction problems, the use of statistical primitives can help to evolve solutions that generalize well across time-series data, but that the same is not necessarily the case when using such primitives for single-step prediction problems.
